meta.title: The Measuring Corner
meta.textType: a science text with key words

paragraphs: The Measuring Corner, posted by Mia. On Saturday, the Explorers went to the Measuring Corner in the science museum. A sign at the door said, "Welcome to the Measuring Corner." Guide Ann gave each of us a small guidebook. The corner was a bright room with three long tables. Many children from other schools were there too. The guidebook has pictures of three tools. It says, "A fact is something that you can measure." We learned about temperature, how heavy a thing is, and time.

The first tool was a thermometer. It is a thin glass tube with a red line inside. It tells us the temperature. We measure temperature in degrees. Ice melts at zero degrees, and water boils at one hundred degrees. Guide Ann put the thermometer in a cup of cold water. It showed ten degrees. Then she put it in a cup of warm water, and the number went up. Leo put his hand in the cold cup and shouted, "It is cold!"

The second tool was a pair of scales. Scales tell us how heavy a thing is. We measure it in grams. A small egg is about sixty grams. Guide Ann put an egg on the scales, and the number was sixty. My camera was much heavier than the egg. Guide Ann put a small stone on the scales, and the number was one hundred. May put her notebook on the scales, and it was not as heavy as my camera.

The third tool was a big clock. A clock has a long hand for minutes and a short hand for hours. Guide Ann said, "A moment is a very short time." She asked us to clap once every second. At the same moment, the Explorers counted to ten. We clapped ten times, and the clock showed ten seconds. Mia and May laughed because Leo clapped too fast.

At the end, Guide Ann asked, "Which tool do you like best?" In my opinion, the scales are the best, because they are easy to read. Leo said, "In my opinion, the thermometer is better." May chose the clock, because she likes numbers. An opinion is not a fact, because nobody can measure it. Guide Ann smiled, and she said, "Every answer is good." We all thanked Guide Ann, and we kept the guidebook.
text.summary: Mia writes about the Measuring Corner in the science museum. Guide Ann shows three tools: a thermometer for the temperature in degrees, scales for the weight in grams, and a clock for a moment of time.
